newsitem.title: INDIA: World Bank lends India $53 mln for roads study.
newsitem.headline: World Bank lends India $53 mln for roads study.

text.p: The World Bank has sanctioned a $53 million loan for India to prepare feasibility reports and preliminary studies to help road-building, a spokesman for the bank said on Tuesday.

"The overall objective of this project is to strengthen policy-based efforts by states in India towards effective reforms in provision, financing and maintenance of road infrastructure," the bank said in a statement.

The World Bank was in talks with the government of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh for another loan worth $300 million to build highways, but the necessary appraisals had not been carried out, the World Bank spokesman told Reuters.
"The bank has not decided anything. Appraisals will be made later this year and if they are acceptable the project would be given to the bank's board for approval in June 1997," he said.

He denied a report in the Financial Express daily that said India was in talks to negotiate a $5.0 billion loan to build 13,000 km of highway in 16 states. He said no such single loan was under consideration.

The Financial Express said on Tuesday that the Finance Ministry estimated an average annual inflow of $500 million of World Bank financing over 10 years for state highways. It said the final details of the loan would be discussed at a meeting next week in Washington between Finance Ministry and World Bank officials.
